strategy_title: Fix 1D Grid Bug by Matching XBLOCK to xnumel
strategy_description: When a Triton kernel uses tl.program_id(1) and tl.program_id(2) for Y-dimension indexing but is launched with a 1D grid, program_id(1) and program_id(2) are always 0, causing only the first YBLOCK rows to be processed. The fix is to launch a 3D grid (cdiv(xnumel, XBLOCK), cdiv(ynumel, YBLOCK), 1) without modifying the kernel body. Critically, XBLOCK must equal xnumel (here 64) so that a single X-block covers all channels without waste or over-indexing; prior attempts with XBLOCK != xnumel produced max_diff ~7.0 correctness failures. The modest 4.8% speedup (vs. expected 50-90x) suggests the profiled kernel is still a small-grid case — the correctness fix is the primary value here.
slow_pseudocode:
# kernel uses program_id(0) for X, program_id(1) and program_id(2) for Y
def kernel_function(*inputs):
    xnumel = 64
    ynumel = 2032128
    grid = (triton.cdiv(xnumel, 8),)  # 1D grid of 8 blocks; program_id(1)=0 always
    kernel[grid](..., YBLOCK=8, XBLOCK=128)
fast_pseudocode:
# Fix: 3D grid matching kernel's program_id usage; XBLOCK = xnumel exactly
def kernel_function(*inputs):
    xnumel = 64
    ynumel = 2032128
    XBLOCK = 64   # must equal xnumel to avoid over-indexing
    YBLOCK = 128
    grid = (triton.cdiv(xnumel, XBLOCK), triton.cdiv(ynumel, YBLOCK), 1)
    kernel[grid](..., YBLOCK=YBLOCK, XBLOCK=XBLOCK)
    # kernel body unchanged — store/load index formulas preserved exactly
applicable_when: Triton kernel uses tl.program_id(1) and/or tl.program_id(2) for Y-dimension indexing but kernel_function launches a 1D grid (only program_id(0) is non-trivial). NCU LaunchConfiguration rule fires with grid_size << sm_count and waves_per_sm ~0. Achieved occupancy is very low (e.g. <10%). The xnumel is small and fixed (e.g. 64 channels).
do_not_apply_when: XBLOCK must not be set larger than xnumel — doing so causes correctness failures (max_diff ~7.0) because threads index beyond valid X range. Do not modify the kernel body's index formulas when fixing the grid. Do not add @triton.autotune if the kernel has constexpr tile parameters that must match the grid computation exactly.
framework_notes: Triton-specific: tl.program_id(0), tl.program_id(1), tl.program_id(2) map to grid dimensions 0, 1, 2 respectively. A 1D grid launch sets program_id(1)=program_id(2)=0. The 3D grid must have Z=1 when the kernel uses program_id(2) only as part of a flat Y-offset formula (yoffset = program_id(1)*YBLOCK + program_id(2)*num_programs(1)*YBLOCK). Setting XBLOCK=xnumel ensures cdiv(xnumel, XBLOCK)=1 X-block, covering all X elements in one block.
